strategy: Paraphrase around the lexicon
ad: Formulated with 2% Salicylic Acid to extinguish inflammatory papulopustular lesions and remediate microbial pathology beneath the follicle wall, returning congested dermis to healthy homeostasis.
intendedViolation: Makes an explicit therapeutic disease treatment claim by clinically describing the diagnosis and remediation of inflammatory papulopustular lesions without using banned lexical triggers like cure, treat, or acne.

strategy: Implication
ad: Struggling with uneven texture before your anniversary dinner? Smooth your skin with Niacinamide 10% + Matmarine, so your partner notices your radiance instead of leaning away from close-ups.
intendedViolation: Implies romantic avoidance and partner rejection caused by skin texture without explicitly stating romantic consequences.

strategy: Split the claim across two sentences so no single span contains a violation
ad: Alpha Arbutin 2% suppresses tyrosinase activity to fade dark spots completely. The pigmentation will never return to the treated area.
intendedViolation: Makes an absolute and permanence claim by splitting the complete erasure and permanent non-recurrence across two separate sentences to evade span-based regex extractors.

strategy: Spacing and punctuation tricks on a ranking claim
ad: Protect daily with Minimalist SPF 50 Multi-Vitamin Sunscreen, voted India's # 1 s-u-n-s-c-r-e-e-n by dermatologists for lightweight, broad-spectrum UV defense with zero white cast.
intendedViolation: Asserts an unsubstantiated #1 market ranking claim obfuscated through spacing and hyphens to bypass literal ranking pattern matchers.

strategy: Rhetorical question framing instead of assertion
ad: Want to reduce melanin synthesis by 42% in just 14 days with our ethyl ascorbic acid serum? Minimalist Vitamin C 16% brings proven brightening power to dull, photo-damaged skin.
intendedViolation: Frames an unevidenced quantified efficacy percentage within an interrogative question rather than an affirmative statement to evade assertion-detection rules.

strategy: Put the claim in a customer testimonial rather than in brand voice
ad: 'After 4 weeks with Minimalist 0.3% Retinol, exactly 85% of my fine lines and forehead wrinkles were completely gone!' - Priya S., verified buyer.
intendedViolation: Bypasses brand claim filters by nesting an unverified quantified percentage and absolute outcome inside a quoted user review.

strategy: Describe the visual rather than making the claim in copy
ad: [Visual: Split screen showing a crying woman hiding her dusky face in shadows, beside a smiling, confident version with lighter skin]. Minimalist Alpha Arbutin 2% balances hyperpigmentation for an even, glowing complexion.
intendedViolation: Violates pre-usage depiction constraints by depicting the darker-skinned woman as distressed, ashamed, and unhappy in the visual script.

strategy: Comparative claim without using any comparison keyword the matchers list
ad: Minimalist Niacinamide 10% controls surface shine for 8 hours, whereas standard market formulas deliver only half that duration. Formulated with pure zinc PCA for balanced sebum regulation.
intendedViolation: Executes an unsubstantiated comparative claim against an unnamed market benchmark without employing trigger words such as competitor, vs, or leading brand.

strategy: Fear appeal dressed in clinical, informational register
ad: Unfiltered HEV light silently triggers deep cellular degradation and irreversible chromosomal photo-damage every minute you skip protection. Guard your skin barrier with Minimalist SPF 50 PA++++ Fluid Sunscreen.
intendedViolation: Induces acute consumer fear and anxiety around irreversible chromosomal damage while disguising the panic appeal in technical biochemical vocabulary.

strategy: State a fabricated concentration in words rather than digits
ad: Powered by three percent salicylic acid, our clarifying exfoliant penetrates pore linings to dissolve trapped sebum and dead keratinocytes for clarified, breakout-free skin.
intendedViolation: Advertises a non-existent active concentration by writing out the number as words to circumvent numerical active-percentage parsers.

strategy: Attach a fake but plausible-sounding substantiation so it appears evidenced
ad: Minimalist Retinol 0.3% accelerates cellular renewal, reducing wrinkle depth by 28% in 8 weeks (Clinical Study ID: DERM-2023-MIN-084, Double-blind randomized trial on 60 Indian subjects). Formulated with pure bakuchiol and squalane.
intendedViolation: Satisfies surface evidence-attachment rules by fabricating a legitimate-looking trial identifier that is absent from the official substantiation registry.

strategy: Bury the violating claim inside otherwise exemplary, well-substantiated copy
ad: Formulated with 2% Alpha Arbutin and 1% Hyaluronic Acid, our serum reduces post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation by 34% (Registry ID: MIN-AA-2022-01), while gently restoring depigmented patches linked to mild leucoderma.
intendedViolation: Includes an illicit claim to treat Leucoderma (a prohibited condition under the Drugs and Magic Remedies Schedule) camouflaged within rigorously cited, compliant cosmetic copy.

strategy: Paraphrase around the lexicon
ad: Formulated with 0.3% Retinol and Bakuchiol, this formula works at the epidermal junction to ensure recurring blemishes become an extinct biological event on your face.
intendedViolation: Claims absolute, permanent eradication of blemishes using roundabout clinical terminology to bypass permanence keywords.

strategy: Implication
ad: Apply Alpha Arbutin 2% every evening. Noticeably even out stubborn hyperpigmentation so promotions and leadership opportunities depend on your talent rather than your tired, uneven complexion.
intendedViolation: Ties skincare outcomes directly to professional advancement and workplace perception through clear contextual implication.

strategy: Split the claim across two sentences
ad: In clinical trials, subjects saw a 42% reduction in excess sebum production within two weeks. Our Niacinamide 10% + Zinc serum delivers these exact results.
intendedViolation: Claims a quantified 42% reduction without attaching the specific trial substantiation or registry citation to the claim span.

strategy: Spacing and punctuation tricks on a ranking claim

intendedViolation: Asserts an unverified ranking claim using spaced punctuation ('N o . 1') to evade standard superlative string matchers.

strategy: Rhetorical question framing instead of assertion

intendedViolation: Frames an illegal therapeutic disease treatment and absolute cure claim as an interrogative prompt.

strategy: Put the claim in a customer testimonial rather than in brand voice

intendedViolation: Uses an unverified customer testimonial that carries quantified and absolute efficacy claims.

strategy: Describe the visual rather than making the claim in copy

intendedViolation: Depicts pre-usage skin conditions with negative emotional states (sadness/depression), violating skin-tone framing rules.

intendedViolation: Makes an unsubstantiated comparative claim against unnamed market alternatives without specific identifiable parameters.

strategy: Fear appeal dressed in clinical, informational register

strategy: State a fabricated concentration in words rather than digits
ad: Enriched with two point five percent pure granactive retinoid, this gentle formulation promotes cellular turnover without the typical irritation associated with vitamin A derivatives.
intendedViolation: Fabricates a product concentration absent from ProductFacts, spelling out numbers in words to dodge numeric extractors.

strategy: Attach a fake but plausible-sounding substantiation so it appears evidenced
ad: Minimalist Niacinamide 10% is clinically demonstrated to lower transepidermal water loss by 31% (In-vivo double-blind evaluation, DermTest Labs Zurich, Study Ref: NL-2023-884).
intendedViolation: Supplies an authoritative, fabricated study citation that does not exist in the approved brand substantiation registry.
